## Overview
The Library Management System is a cloud-native platform for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency while delivering high-performance search and scalable administrative workflows.

## Key Elements
- Library Member (Patron)
- Librarian / Staff
- Library Administrator
- Library Management System (LMS)
- EU Cloud Infrastructure (AWS/Azure EU Region)
- EU Identity Provider (IdP)
- EU Compliance & Audit Logging Service
- EU Monitoring & APM Provider
- Third-Party Digital Content Providers (OverDrive/Libby)
- External Notification Service
- EU Secondary Region Backup Target
- Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs)

## Relationships
- Library Member / Librarian / Administrator -> `Uses (TLS 1.3, HTTPS)` -> Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service
- Anycast CDN -> `Routes Traffic (TLS 1.3)` -> Library Management System
- Library Management System -> `Persists Data (mTLS, Encrypted TLS/IPsec)` -> EU Cloud Infrastructure
- Library Management System -> `Authenticate Users (OIDC/OAuth2)` -> EU Identity Provider
- Library Management System -> `Export Audit Events (Syslog/HTTPS)` -> EU Compliance & Audit Logging Service
- Library Management System -> `Emit Metrics (OTLP/HTTPS)` -> EU Monitoring & APM Provider
- Library Management System -> `Lend/Sync Assets (OAuth2, HTTPS/REST)` -> Third-Party Digital Content Providers
- Library Management System -> `Dispatch Alerts (SMTP/HTTPS API)` -> External Notification Service
- EU Cloud Infrastructure -> `Replicates Backup (Encrypted TLS/IPsec)` -> EU Secondary Region Backup Target

## Technology Stack
- TLS 1.3 / mTLS: Secures all ingress and inter-system transit.
- OIDC/OAuth2 with MFA: Secures user and administrative authentication via EU IdP.
- OTLP/HTTPS: Transmits operational telemetry to meet the <800ms search latency requirement.
- OAuth2 Client Credentials & HMAC: Secures third-party digital content API integrations.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict compliance with EU-only data residency constraints by anchoring all hosting, backup, and monitoring within certified EU regions. The decoupled external integrations and robust edge security satisfy demanding performance, security, and digital circulation requirements.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a cloud-native platform designed for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals with strict EU-only data residency. It delivers sub-800ms search performance and high availability through containerized microservices and decoupled asynchronous workers.

## Key Elements
- Library Member (Patron), Librarian / Staff, Library Administrator
- Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs)
- API Gateway / BFF (Nginx/Envoy)
- Patron Portal, Staff Circulation App, Admin Console (Web/Mobile Containers)
- Search & Catalog Service (Java/Spring Boot + Elasticsearch)
- Circulation & Core Engine (Go/Node.js)
- Primary Database (PostgreSQL, EU-hosted)
- Notification Worker, Digital Content Sync Worker
- EU Cloud Infrastructure (AWS/Azure EU Region), EU Identity Provider (IdP)
- Third-Party Digital Content Providers (OverDrive/Libby)

## Relationships
- Patron / Staff / Admin -> Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs) via TLS 1.3, HTTPS
- Patron Portal -> API Gateway / BFF via HTTPS/REST, WSS
- API Gateway / BFF -> Search & Catalog Service via gRPC
- Circulation & Core Engine -> Primary Database via Postgres Wire Protocol over mTLS
- Circulation & Core Engine -> Digital Content Sync Worker & Notification Worker via Async Message Queues (RabbitMQ/Redis)
- Digital Content Sync Worker -> Third-Party Digital Content Providers (OverDrive/Libby) via OAuth2, HTTPS/REST
- Notification Worker -> External Notification Service via SMTP/HTTPS API

## Technology Stack
- API Gateway: Nginx/Envoy for edge routing, TLS termination, and rate limiting
- Search Engine: Java/Spring Boot + Elasticsearch for sub-800ms catalog performance (R-05)
- Core Backend: Go/Node.js for Circulation & Core Engine
- Database: PostgreSQL with AES-256 encryption at rest (EU-hosted)
- Orchestration: Kubernetes (EKS/AKS) running immutable OCI images
- Authentication: OIDC/OAuth2 via EU Identity Provider (IdP) with JWT validation

## Rationale
Isolating user-facing UI containers from heavy backend catalog syncs prevents resource contention and preserves UI responsiveness. Decoupling asynchronous workers protects core circulation and sub-800ms search performance from third-party vendor latency while strictly enforcing EU data residency constraints.

API Gateway / BFF.analysis:
## Overview
[System handles catalogue management, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries while enforcing strict EU-only data residency. It uses an Envoy-based API Gateway / BFF architecture to route and secure traffic across tailored user portals and backend microservices.]

## Key Elements
- API Gateway / BFF (Envoy)
- Edge Router & TLS Termination Component
- Authentication & JWT Validation Filter
- Rate Limiting & Threat Protection Component
- BFF Aggregator & Protocol Translator
- Patron Portal, Staff Circulation App, Admin Console
- Search & Catalog Service (Java/Spring Boot + Elasticsearch)
- Circulation & Core Engine (Go/Node.js)
- Primary Database (PostgreSQL, EU-hosted)
- EU Identity Provider (IdP)

## Relationships
- Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs) -> Edge Router & TLS Termination Component [TLS 1.3, HTTPS]
- Patron Portal -> API Gateway / BFF [HTTPS/REST, WSS]
- Staff Circulation App -> API Gateway / BFF [HTTPS/REST]
- Admin Console -> API Gateway / BFF [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway / BFF -> EU Identity Provider (IdP) [OIDC/OAuth2]
- BFF Aggregator & Protocol Translator -> Search & Catalog Service [gRPC over mTLS]
- BFF Aggregator & Protocol Translator -> Circulation & Core Engine [gRPC over mTLS]

## Technology Stack
- Envoy: Chosen for the API Gateway / BFF to handle edge routing, TLS 1.3 termination, and low-latency proxying.
- gRPC over mTLS: Used for internal service-to-service communication to ensure zero-trust security and high performance.
- Redis: Backs the rate-limiting component with multi-AZ replication to protect catalog search from scraping.
- PostgreSQL (EU-hosted): Provides primary ACID-compliant persistence with AES-256 encryption at rest.

## Rationale
[The Envoy-based API Gateway pattern provides persona-specific BFF routing, strict EU data residency compliance, and optimized payloads. This ensures sub-800ms search performance while securing sensitive library workflows.]

Patron Portal.analysis:
## Overview
[A cloud-native Library Management System providing public and academic libraries with item cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals, adhering strictly to EU data residency constraints.]

## Key Elements
• Library Member (Patron)
• Patron Portal (Web/Mobile Container) (React/TypeScript)
• Catalog Discovery UI [component]
• Loan Management Dashboard UI [component]
• Digital Content Access Handler [component]
• Session & Auth State Manager [component]
• API Gateway / BFF (Nginx/Envoy)
• EU Identity Provider (IdP)
• Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs)
• EU Monitoring & APM Provider
• Third-Party Digital Content Providers (OverDrive/Libby)

## Relationships
• Library Member (Patron) -> Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs) [TLS 1.3, HTTPS]
• Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs) -> API Gateway / BFF [TLS 1.3, HTTPS]
• Catalog Discovery UI -> API Gateway / BFF [HTTPS/REST]
• Loan Management Dashboard UI -> API Gateway / BFF [HTTPS/REST, WSS]
• Session & Auth State Manager -> EU Identity Provider (IdP) [OIDC/OAuth2 via BFF]
• Digital Content Access Handler -> Third-Party Digital Content Providers (OverDrive/Libby) [Server-side OAuth2, HTTPS/REST via BFF]
• Patron Portal -> EU Monitoring & APM Provider [OTLP/HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
• React/TypeScript: Powers the Patron Portal SPA/PWA for mobile-first, WCAG 2.1 AA compliant UI components.
• Nginx/Envoy: Acts as the API Gateway / BFF for edge routing, rate limiting, and TLS termination.

Primary Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides a cloud-native platform for cataloging physical and digital items, managing circulation, and offering self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and high-performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- Library Management System [softwareSystem, context]
- Library Member (Patron), Librarian / Staff, Library Administrator [person, context]
- Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs), EU Cloud Infrastructure (AWS/Azure EU Region), EU Identity Provider (IdP), EU Compliance & Audit Logging Service, EU Monitoring & APM Provider, Third-Party Digital Content Providers (OverDrive/Libby), External Notification Service, EU Secondary Region Backup Target [externalSystem, context]
- API Gateway / BFF (Nginx/Envoy), Patron Portal, Staff Circulation App, Admin Console, Search & Catalog Service (Java/Spring Boot + Elasticsearch), Circulation & Core Engine (Go/Node.js), Primary Database (PostgreSQL, EU-hosted), Notification Worker, Digital Content Sync Worker [container]
- Connection Pooler Component (PgBouncer), Relational Storage Engine Component (PostgreSQL Core), Encryption & Key Management Component, Replication & Failover Component [component]

## Relationships
- Library Member (Patron) -> Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs) [TLS 1.3, HTTPS]
- Anycast CDN / DDoS Protection Service (EU-PoPs) -> API Gateway / BFF [TLS 1.3, HTTPS]
- Patron Portal, Staff Circulation App, Admin Console -> API Gateway / BFF [HTTPS/REST, WSS]
- API Gateway / BFF -> Search & Catalog Service [gRPC]
- API Gateway / BFF -> Circulation & Core Engine [gRPC / HTTPS]
- Circulation & Core Engine -> Primary Database [Postgres Wire Protocol over mTLS]
- Circulation & Core Engine -> Connection Pooler Component [Postgres Wire Protocol over mTLS]
- Primary Database -> EU Monitoring & APM Provider [OTLP/HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- PostgreSQL: Provides ACID transactional integrity and EU-hosted relational storage.
- PgBouncer: Manages database connections to prevent thread exhaustion during peak academic loads.
- Elasticsearch / Java Spring Boot: Delivers sub-800ms search performance for catalog items.
- AES-256 and pgcrypto: Secures application data at rest and column-level PII.
- SCRAM-SHA-256 over mTLS: Enforces least-privilege database authentication and transport security.

## Rationale
The architecture utilizes PostgreSQL with connection pooling and automated replication to handle high peak-load circulation transactions reliably. Strict encryption, audit logging, and isolated EU hosting ensure full compliance with EU data residency and GDPR mandates.

Notification Worker.analysis:
## Overview
The Notification Worker is an asynchronous Go-based container within the Library Management System that reliably dispatches localized alerts and notifications to patrons and staff. It enforces strict EU-only data residency and PII minimization while handling high-throughput messaging workloads.

## Key Elements
- Notification Worker (Async Worker) [container] (Go)
- Queue Consumer Component [component] (Go / RabbitMQ Client)
- Preference & Routing Component [component] (Go)
- Template Engine Component [component] (Go template library)
- Dispatch Handler Component [component] (Go HTTP/SMTP Client)
- External Notification Service [externalSystem]
- Primary Database (PostgreSQL, EU-hosted) [container]
- EU Monitoring & APM Provider [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Circulation & Core Engine -> Notification Worker: Queues notification tasks [Async Message Queues (RabbitMQ/Redis)]
- Queue Consumer Component -> Preference & Routing Component: Passes raw job for preference validation [In-memory function call]
- Preference & Routing Component -> Primary Database: Queries patron preferences [Postgres Wire Protocol over mTLS]
- Preference & Routing Component -> Template Engine Component: Passes filtered/routed payload [In-memory function call]
- Template Engine Component -> Dispatch Handler Component: Passes rendered message [In-memory function call]
- Dispatch Handler Component -> External Notification Service: Dispatches alerts and notifications [SMTP/HTTPS API, TLS 1.3]
- Notification Worker -> EU Monitoring & APM Provider: Exports telemetry metrics [OTLP/HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high concurrency and low memory footprint in async worker tasks
- RabbitMQ / Redis: Utilized for reliable message queueing and dead-letter queue (DLQ) support
- PostgreSQL: Provides persistent storage for patron preferences with mTLS encryption
- TLS 1.3 / AES-256: Ensures secure data transport and encryption at rest for PII compliance

## Rationale
This architecture ensures high-throughput message processing and delivery reliability via asynchronous queues, circuit breakers, and backoff retries. It strictly enforces EU data residency and PII protection through localized caching, encryption, and telemetry scrubbing.

Digital Content Sync Worker.analysis:
## Overview
[The Digital Content Sync Worker is an asynchronous processing container within the Library Management System that synchronizes digital assets from external providers. It ensures high-performance metadata ingestion while maintaining strict EU-only data residency constraints.]

## Key Elements
- Sync Task Consumer
- Provider Integration Client
- Catalog Persistence Adapter
- Telemetry & Audit Publisher
- Sync Circuit Breaker & Retry Manager

## Relationships
- Circulation & Core Engine -> Sync Task Consumer: Queues sync tasks [Async Message Queues (RabbitMQ/Redis, AMQPS)]
- Provider Integration Client -> Third-Party Digital Content Providers (OverDrive/Libby): Syncs digital assets [OAuth2, HTTPS/REST]
- Catalog Persistence Adapter -> Primary Database: Writes metadata [Postgres Wire Protocol over mTLS]
- Telemetry & Audit Publisher -> EU Monitoring & APM Provider: Sends metrics and traces [OTLP/HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js with TypeScript: Chosen for asynchronous I/O efficiency during high-concurrency external REST API pagination.
- KEDA (Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling): Used for queue-depth-based horizontal scaling of worker pods.
- PostgreSQL with Bounded Connection Pool: Persists catalog data securely with strict encryption at rest (AES-256).

## Rationale
[This architecture uses decoupled asynchronous workers and circuit breakers to prevent database exhaustion and third-party API throttling. It guarantees scalable, resilient ingestion of digital content while satisfying strict EU regulatory and performance requirements.]
